verdict: Norfolk Southern posted record quarterly revenue of $3.5B, up 14% on higher fuel surcharges and 3% more freight, and grew net income to $759M despite merger-related and Eastern Ohio costs.

kpis.label: EPS (GAAP diluted)
kpis.note: vs $3.16 a year ago; adjusted EPS was $3.62

kpis.label: Operating ratio
kpis.note: Operating costs per revenue dollar; 65.4% adjusted

kpis.label: Volume
kpis.note: More carloads and containers than a year ago

segments.name: Merchandise
segments.note: Manufactured goods, chemicals, metals, autos and farm products hauled by rail — the biggest business, up 11%.

segments.name: Intermodal
segments.note: Shipping containers and truck trailers moved by rail — the fastest growth, up 21% as a tighter trucking market pushed freight to rail.

segments.name: Coal
segments.note: Coal for power plants, steelmaking and export — up 12%.

opex.name: Depreciation
opex.note: Wear and tear on locomotives, track and equipment, spread over their working lives.

otherDetail: Other expense of $163M, net: $193M of interest expense on the railroad's debt, partly offset by $30M of other income.
follow100Note: Cost of revenue breaks down as compensation and benefits $753M, purchased services and rents $546M, fuel $420M, materials and other $224M, merger-related expenses $42M and Eastern Ohio incident costs $28M. Depreciation is the only remaining operating-expense line, so revenue less total railway operating expenses equals the reported $1,150M income from railway operations.

takeaways.title: Record revenue — much of it fuel surcharges
takeaways.text: Revenue hit a record $3,526M, up 14%. Volume rose 3%, and higher fuel surcharges — extra charges that rise with diesel prices — contributed eight of the fourteen points of growth.

takeaways.title: Intermodal is the growth story
takeaways.text: Intermodal revenue jumped 21% to $919M and merchandise 11% to $2,188M, as a tighter trucking market made rail more attractive. Coal rose 12% to $419M.

takeaways.title: Fuel costs squeezed the operating ratio
takeaways.text: The operating ratio — operating costs per dollar of revenue — was 67.4%, worse than a year ago, because fuel expense jumped 77% to $420M and the quarter carried $42M of merger-related and $28M of Eastern Ohio incident costs. Excluding those items the ratio was 65.4%.

oneTimers: $42M of merger-related expenses and $28M of Eastern Ohio incident costs are inside this quarter's operating expenses. Excluding them (and year-ago items), adjusted income from railway operations was $1.2B and adjusted EPS was $3.62 instead of $3.37.
footerNote: Railroads do not report gross profit; cost of revenue here = direct train-running costs, following the same treatment as the CSX page.
